runs.note: re-verified after the LayerNormalization bias patch; the Node gate also still passes

runs.error: kernel error resolved by adding an explicit 1-D zero bias to every LayerNormalization; the session now runs
runs.reading: The graph executes on WebGPU but decodes to word salad while WASM in the same browser and CPU in Node both match the oracle exactly. This is a numerical divergence on the WebGPU execution provider, not a load or shape failure, and it is the same class of defect already recorded for another model in this repository.

runs.fix_applied: tools/moonshine-onnx-export/add_layernorm_bias.py adds an explicit zero bias so the WebGPU SkipLayerNormalization fusion binds a 1-D beta. Numerically neutral: an absent bias and a zero bias mean the same.
runs.remaining: the divergence itself is not fixed; it needs stage-level comparison to locate the first differing tensor

runs.error: RangeError: WebAssembly.Memory(): Property 'initial': value 109143 is above the upper bound 65536
runs.reading: the graphs load once their external-data sidecars are mounted, but the session asks for 109143 WASM pages, about 6.99 GB, against a 65536 page ceiling of 4 GB.
runs.conclusion: A 0.6B fp32 model is not browser-shippable. Both execution providers fail the same way, so this is not a provider choice. Enabling WASM memory growth cannot help because the initial allocation itself exceeds the 4 GB WASM32 address space.
runs.caveat: the Qwen browser case feeds the captured mel features because the library frontend is not wired, so it would measure the graphs rather than the frontend even if it loaded.
runs.webgpu_check: run separately and it fails identically, so GPU memory does not help: ORT allocates the graph linear memory for weights regardless of the execution provider

harness_changes: Moonshine now points at the migrated artifact set and mounts each graph's external-data sidecar, because a blob URL gives ORT no directory to resolve them against.
A qwen3asr case was added with the same sidecar mounting and an explicit memory-growth attempt.

The Moonshine loader was still passing seedCache after the session migration retired that architecture; it now uses the cross-attention graph and reads the past-state geometry from the export receipt.
honest_note: Only the Moonshine WASM run is a pass. The WebGPU kernel failure and the Qwen memory ceiling are real browser constraints, measured with exact numbers rather than inferred.
